solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: More than one studio needed to get such an enterprise rolling?

definitions.text: More than one studio needed to get such an enterprise rolling?

parts.words: More than one studio needed to get such an enterprise rolling?
parts.note: a film made by several studios together is a shared venture; read the other way, rolling a cannabis cigarette is getting a joint going

explanation.surface: A film producer muses that a big project needs several studios to get it under way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling' is both the film-set cue to start shooting and what you do to a joint, a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-operative film or show made by several companies together is described by exactly this two-word phrase.

clue.text: Not hard for chap having a whale of a time round an east end piano

indicators.note: round means the shortened name goes around the next piece
not hard tells us to drop the letter for hard, as on pencils, from the chap's name

parts.words: chap having a whale of a time
parts.note: Jonah, the biblical prophet swallowed by a whale
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man enjoying himself enormously around an old piano in a London pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not hard' drops the pencil letter for hard from the prophet's name. London's East End is the home of Cockney rhyming slang, where this name rhymes roughly with 'pianner'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang a piano is a joanna, from the rough rhyme with 'pianner'.

clue.text: Bugged — without silence, didn't work

indicators.note: without means the word for quiet is removed from the word for dodging work

parts.note: to shirk is to avoid work, so shirked means didn't work
sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A spy device was planted, but without quiet surroundings it failed to function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bugged' looks like a spy's listening device, but it is the definition in the sense of annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is informal for to annoy or irritate them, so bugged is a synonym.

clue.text: See 27
Regarded as fair, like a shot it's OK to take again just one time?

indicators.note: just one says only one of the doubled time letters stays, so one is dropped

parts.words: like a shot it's OK to take again
parts.note: a putt you may play again would be re-puttable, with two Ts

explanation.surface: A golfer asks whether a stroke may fairly be replayed just once.
explanation.walkthrough: The whimsical RE-PUTTABLE (able to be putted again) has two Ts; 'just one time' keeps only one T.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a good name, respected and trusted, is well regarded and thought honest.

clue.text: Doctor accepting a kebab

indicators.note: accepting means the doctor's letters take another piece inside them

parts.note: a means one, a single thing

explanation.surface: A physician takes a kebab, perhaps as a late-night snack or a bribe.
explanation.definitionFit: Doner is the Turkish-style kebab of meat sliced from a vertical rotating spit.

clue.text: Spurn day-old lamb?

definitions.meaning: to spurn someone is to snub them or treat them with deliberate coldness
joint of lamb from the forelimb served ... the next day, as leftovers

explanation.surface: A cook refuses to serve yesterday's leftover lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Day-old lamb' is read as a newborn animal, but it is leftover meat: the joint cooked yesterday and now eaten cold.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the snub is an idiom for deliberately ignoring them; the meat sense is literal leftovers.

clue.text: Current Number One, tennis's top ace Henman on the way up … it's not for real

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: on the way up in a down clue means the following pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: top picks the first letter of the word tennis

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
Tim Henman, the British tennis player

explanation.surface: A sports report hails a British tennis star climbing to world number one, then admits it's fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the way up' reads everything after 'Current' from the bottom, giving MITATION. Tim Henman was a much-loved British player who never reached world number one, hence 'not for real'.
explanation.definitionFit: A copy or fake is something not genuine, so a counterfeit is not for real.

clue.text: Incorrect posture regularly adopted in evening

indicators.note: adopted in means those letters are taken into the word for evening

parts.note: night is a synonym for evening

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word posture, starting from the second

explanation.surface: An etiquette note: slouching at an evening event is bad form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of POSTURE, giving OTR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wrong or mistaken is incorrect, the plain negation of being correct.

clue.text: Berlin takes disturbed kids

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: The German capital takes in troubled children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Berlin' looks like a city or a person, but it is just letters to rearrange with TAKES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankle-biters is a jokey informal name for small children, who are about ankle height.

clue.text: TV personality delivers lines pat — canned laughter's beginning

indicators.note: canned is slang for drunk, so these letters are reeling into a new order
beginning picks the first letter of the word laughter

explanation.surface: A television celebrity reels off glib lines, starting the canned laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canned' looks like it describes recorded laughter, but it is the anagram signal, slang for drunk; L, the start of 'laughter', joins LINESPAT in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a quiz or chat-show panel is a familiar television figure.

clue.text: River flowing quietly westward in sleepy land

indicators.note: westward in an across clue means the river's name is read right to left

parts.note: the Don, from the Sholokhov novel And Quiet Flows the Don

explanation.surface: A river meanders gently towards the west through a drowsy countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: The land of Nod is a jokey idiom for sleep, borrowed from the biblical land east of Eden.

clue.text: See 9
Authoritarian Spaniard, insular type, back after dropping international school exam

indicators.note: after dropping means the exam letters are removed once the word is turned round
back means the islander's word is read in reverse

parts.note: an Ibizan is a native of the Spanish island of Ibiza
the IB, the International Baccalaureate

explanation.surface: A strict Spanish islander returns after quitting an international exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' gives NAZIBI; 'after dropping' then removes the exam letters from its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Used loosely, the label for a Hitler party member describes any overbearing, dictatorial person.

clue.text: Be in the same social network as wits who burble inanely

definitions.text: Be in the same social network as

indicators.note: inanely means the words are jumbled senselessly into a new order

explanation.surface: Mixing with comedians who prattle on foolishly, perhaps on social media.
explanation.definitionFit: To mingle socially with people, meeting them in the same circles, is this idiom.

clue.text: Capital increasing by itself when account's maintained

parts.note: up means increasing, as prices are up

indicators.note: maintained means held inside, so the account letters sit within the Latin phrase

parts.note: per se is Latin for by itself
C/A is the banking abbreviation for current account

explanation.surface: Capital that grows on its own while an account is kept open, a banker's dream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks financial, as do 'increasing' and 'account', but it means a capital letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A capital letter is one in the large-letter set used by typesetters, as opposed to small letters.

clue.text: American arms grew uncontrollably, say Pentagon strategists

indicators.note: uncontrollably means the letters run wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: US weapons stocks have swollen out of control, according to military planners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks the definition as an example: Pentagon planners are one kind of people who play simulated battles.
explanation.definitionFit: Military planners rehearse conflicts through simulated battles, so they play at mock combat exercises.

clue.text: See 14
Unusual Australian puts play on

indicators.note: unusual means the letters appear in an unexpected order, rearranged

explanation.surface: An eccentric Aussie stages a theatrical production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' does double duty in spirit: it signals the rearrangement and describes the egg-laying mammal.
explanation.definitionFit: The duck-billed, egg-laying mammal is native to eastern Australia.

clue.text: See 6
Surgical procedure making cheek round

parts.note: lip means cheek, as in insolent talk
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A cosmetic operation that gives someone fuller, rounder cheeks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheek' looks like part of the face being reshaped, but it means impudence.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for liposuction, the cosmetic operation that removes body fat.

clue.text: Skin disease endlessly returning between ram's head and bottom — get tick off

indicators.note: head picks the first letter of the word ram
returning means the shortened disease is read backwards
endlessly removes the final letter of the disease

parts.note: herpes is a viral skin infection
end means bottom, the far extremity

explanation.surface: A vet notes a skin complaint spreading from a ram's head to its rear, and must remove a tick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' gives HERPE and 'returning' makes EPREH, which sits 'between' the ram's head and the bottom. 'Tick off' is the definition, not a parasite to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: To tick someone off is informal for to scold them, a synonym of rebuke.

clue.text: Queen of hearts tucking into frozen tart

indicators.note: tucking into means the suit letter goes inside the word for frozen water

parts.note: ice is frozen water
H is the card-suit abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: The Queen of Hearts, of nursery-rhyme tart fame, eats a chilled pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme's Queen of Hearts made some tarts, which makes 'tart' look part of that story; here it defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A savoury open pastry case filled with egg custard is a kind of flan or tart.

clue.text: Newspaper covering sport backing racing

indicators.note: backing means the assembled letters are read in reverse
covering means the paper's letters go round the sport's

parts.note: the FT, the Financial Times
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A newspaper's sports coverage supports horse racing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covering' makes FRUT, which 'backing' turns round; 'racing' looks like the sport covered, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The turf is a standard name for horse racing as a sport, from the grass tracks.

clue.text: Stuck in mud, an axle's flipped over in poet's city

indicators.note: flipped over means the lodged letters are read in reverse
stuck in means the answer is lodged within the words mud, an axle

explanation.surface: A car stuck in mud overturns on the way to the city of a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge's poem Kubla Khan opens with the pleasure-dome in the city Kubla built.

clue.text: Do I have authorisation to proceed, pal?

parts.note: the question 'do I have' is recast as 'am I', as in 'am I (given the) go'
a go is the signal or permission to go ahead

explanation.surface: Someone checks with a friend whether they have the green light.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as the question 'Am I go?', meaning 'have I got the go-ahead?'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish word for friend is widely used in English for a mate or buddy.

clue.text: Vintage, mostly worthless rubbish

indicators.note: mostly means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: crud is slang for dirt or worthless rubbish

explanation.surface: An old wine dismissed as almost entirely worthless junk.
explanation.definitionFit: A cru is a vineyard or its wine of recognised quality, as in grand cru.

clue.text: Dog that's amazing set on soldier

indicators.note: set on in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: cor! is a British exclamation of amazement
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An astonishing dog is sicked onto a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set on' suggests a dog attacking, but it places COR above GI in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh breed of short-legged herding dog is famous as the royal family's favourite.

clue.text: Encounter between upright individuals which may lead to 1 of 9,12?

definitions.text: Encounter between upright individuals which may lead to 1 of 9,12?

parts.words: Encounter between upright individuals which may lead to 1 of 9,12?
parts.note: upright suggests respectable people but means standing; the encounter is sex standing up, which may produce one small child

explanation.surface: A meeting of virtuous people that might end with one of the toddlers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright' seems to mean honourable but means standing. 9,12 is ANKLE BITERS, small children; '1 of' them is a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a hurried sexual encounter while standing up, which might well lead to pregnancy.

clue.text: Maybe weeping tree, say, one's put outside institute

indicators.note: put outside means the plant's letters are placed round the institute's

parts.note: a tree is an example of a plant
one's, read as one has, becomes I've

explanation.surface: A weeping willow, perhaps, that someone has planted outside an institute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weeping' and 'tree' suggest a weeping willow, but 'Maybe weeping' is the definition. 'One's' stands for 'one has', which becomes I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mournful and sad-sounding, as weeping sounds; weeping is one example of such a cry.

clue.text: Column's style and hairdo tips costly, for the most part

parts.note: a do is informal for a hairdo

indicators.note: for the most part means only most of the word is used, dropping its last letter

parts.note: rich can mean costly or sumptuous

explanation.surface: A hair salon's styling advice: tips, mostly expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips' links the pieces, saying the hairdo leans towards costly.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the classical Greek orders of architecture, with plain capitals on its columns.

clue.text: Emergency transport of bone china?

parts.note: a skeleton is the bony frame, bones collectively
a service is a set of matching china dishes

explanation.surface: Delicate bone china that needs urgent shipping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bone china' reads as one thing, fine porcelain, but splits into bone and china.
explanation.definitionFit: A pared-down timetable, run by minimal staff in a strike or crisis, is a skeleton service.
